stem: Amlodipine besylate (Norvasc) is a calcium channel blocker that must be monitored carefully in elderly patients MOST because of which risk?
options: Some elderly, especially those with severe obstructive coronary artery disease, have developed increased frequency, duration, or severity of angina or acute myocardial infarction after initiation or at time of dosage increase
A complete absence of any cardiovascular risk regardless of dosage change
An immediate and permanent cure of coronary artery disease
A guaranteed decrease in blood pressure with no risk of hypotension

stem: Which nursing action is recommended regarding blood pressure monitoring during initiation or dosage increase of amlodipine besylate?
options: Monitor blood pressure frequently during initiation of therapy because the drug may induce vasodilation and a gradual onset of acute hypotensive effect
Monitor blood pressure only once per month regardless of dosage change
Avoid monitoring blood pressure since amlodipine has no hemodynamic effect
Monitor only heart rate with no attention to blood pressure

stem: Which finding should prompt an elderly client taking amlodipine besylate to notify the doctor?
options: Signs of heart failure, including swelling of fingers and feet or shortness of breath
Mild improvement in exercise tolerance with no other symptoms
A single normal blood pressure reading taken at a routine visit
Improved appetite with no other associated symptom

stem: With Nifedipine (Adalat), the nurse should NOT give immediate release formulations in which specific clinical situation?
options: Acute myocardial infarction or acute coronary syndrome
Chronic stable hypertension with no acute cardiac event
Routine outpatient follow-up with no chest pain
A client who has not taken the medication before

stem: Which specific warning applies to an elderly patient taking nifedipine who is also on an antianginal agent, regarding chest pain?
options: Chest pain may worsen briefly when beginning the drug or when dosage is increased
Chest pain is guaranteed to resolve permanently within the first dose
Nifedipine has no association whatsoever with chest pain patterns
Chest pain will only occur if the drug is discontinued abruptly

stem: What specific instruction should be given to an elderly client regarding the extended-release tablet formulation of nifedipine?
options: Instruct the client to swallow the extended-release tablet without breaking or chewing it
Instruct the client to crush the tablet to speed absorption
Instruct the client to chew the tablet thoroughly before swallowing
Instruct the client to dissolve the tablet in water before taking it

stem: Which dietary caution should be given to an elderly client taking nifedipine?
options: Advise the elderly to avoid taking the drug with grapefruit juice
Advise the elderly to take the drug exclusively with grapefruit juice to enhance absorption
Advise the elderly that dietary citrus has no interaction with nifedipine
Advise the elderly to take the drug only with dairy products

stem: With Nitroglycerin, which vital sign requires close monitoring during administration, especially blood pressure in patients with myocardial infarction?
options: Blood pressure
Body temperature exclusively with no attention to blood pressure
Respiratory rate exclusively with no attention to blood pressure
Deep tendon reflexes exclusively

stem: What should the nurse inform the elderly client that nitroglycerin may cause, especially at the beginning of therapy?
options: Headaches
Permanent hearing loss
Immediate improvement in vision
Complete absence of any side effect

stem: Which medication is recommended to be used in conjunction with nitroglycerin for the treatment of headache, according to the notes?
options: Acetaminophen
Aspirin exclusively with no mention of acetaminophen
An opioid analgesic as first-line therapy
No medication, since the headache should simply be tolerated

stem: How should an elderly client be advised to rise after taking nitroglycerin, to minimize dizziness?
options: Advise the client to go up and down stairs carefully and slowly to minimize dizziness when standing up
Advise the client to stand up abruptly to test for dizziness
Advise the client that dizziness cannot occur with nitroglycerin
Advise the client to avoid all stairs permanently regardless of symptoms

stem: Which class of drugs requires the nurse to check the apical pulse before administration, withholding the dose if the pulse is slower than 60 beats per minute?
options: Beta blockers (e.g., Atenolol)
ACE inhibitors (e.g., Captopril)
Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
Alpha blockers (e.g., Doxazosin)

stem: Why should beta blockers be withdrawn gradually in elderly patients, rather than stopped abruptly?
options: To avoid thyroid storm in patients with suspected hyperthyroidism, since beta blockers may mask tachycardia caused by hyperthyroidism
Because abrupt withdrawal of beta blockers has no physiological consequence
Because gradual withdrawal increases the risk of bradycardia with no other benefit
Because abrupt withdrawal always improves thyroid function immediately

stem: Which instruction should the nurse give to the family of an elderly client on beta blockers regarding home monitoring?
options: Teach the elderly or family how to take his/her pulse and blood pressure at home
Instruct the family to avoid any home monitoring since it is unnecessary
Instruct the family to withhold the drug permanently if the first dose is well tolerated
Instruct the family that home monitoring is only necessary for elderly patients taking ACE inhibitors

stem: With Captopril (an ACE inhibitor), what should the nurse monitor regarding blood pressure in elderly patients, considering they may be more sensitive to drug hypotensive effects?
options: Monitor the BP of the elderly and must know that elderly patients may be more sensitive to drug hypotensive effects
Avoid monitoring blood pressure since ACE inhibitors have no hypotensive effect in the elderly
Monitor only heart rate with no attention to blood pressure in patients taking captopril
Assume elderly patients are uniformly less sensitive to captopril's hypotensive effects than younger adults

stem: Which laboratory values should be monitored before starting captopril and every 2 weeks for the first 3 months of therapy, according to the notes?
options: WBC and differential counts
Only fasting blood glucose with no attention to white cell counts
Only serum calcium with no attention to white cell counts
Only urinalysis for glucose with no attention to white cell counts

stem: Which dietary timing instruction should be given to an elderly client taking captopril, regarding food and absorption?
options: Advise the client to take the drug 1 hour before meals because food in the GI tract may reduce absorption
Advise the client to take the drug only with a heavy meal to enhance absorption
Advise the client that food has no effect whatsoever on captopril absorption
Advise the client to take the drug exclusively at bedtime with a snack

stem: What should the nurse inform the client is possible during the first few days of captopril therapy, instructing the client to rise slowly to minimize this effect?
options: Light-headedness
Permanent hearing loss
Immediate and complete resolution of hypertension with no further monitoring needed
Enhanced appetite with no other associated symptom

stem: If fainting occurs in an elderly client taking captopril, what instruction should the client be given?
options: He/she should stop the drug and advise the client to use caution in hot weather
Continue the drug at a higher dose regardless of fainting
Ignore the fainting episode since it is not clinically significant
Discontinue only if fainting occurs more than ten times in a single day

stem: Diarrhea and excessive perspiration in an elderly client on captopril can lead to which of the following?
options: Light-headedness and syncope
A guaranteed increase in blood pressure with no risk of hypotension
Complete resolution of hypertension with no further intervention needed
An isolated effect limited strictly to the gastrointestinal tract with no cardiovascular impact

stem: Which symptoms related to infection should the elderly client taking captopril be instructed to report, given the risk of altered white blood cell counts?
options: Fever and sore throat as well as swelling of face, lips, or mouth or difficulty in breathing
Improved appetite with no other associated symptom
A single episode of mild fatigue with no other symptom
Enhanced energy level with no other associated symptom

stem: With Doxazosin (Cardura), an alpha blocker, what should the nurse monitor closely after starting the drug, given the risk of syncope?
options: Monitor BP closely after starting the drug, if syncope occurs the client should be placed in a recumbent position and treated supportively
Monitor only serum potassium with no attention to blood pressure
Monitor only respiratory rate with no attention to blood pressure or syncope risk
Avoid monitoring blood pressure since doxazosin has no hypotensive effect

stem: The elderly taking doxazosin should be made to know that he/she is susceptible to which specific adverse drug effect, common with all alpha blockers?
options: A first-dose effect, such as marked hypotension or syncope with the initial dose
A guaranteed absence of any adverse effect with the first dose
An automatic improvement in blood pressure with no risk of hypotension
A permanent cure of hypertension after a single dose

stem: The client on doxazosin is advised to avoid which activities until the drug's effects on the central nervous system are known?
options: Driving and other hazardous activities
Routine light walking with no restriction
Reading printed material with no restriction
Eating a balanced diet with no restriction

stem: With Hydralazine hydrochloride, which vital signs should the nurse monitor to reduce sodium retention and tachycardia?
options: BP, pulse rate, and body weight frequently
Only deep tendon reflexes with no attention to BP or pulse
Only respiratory rate with no attention to BP or pulse
Only temperature with no attention to BP or pulse

stem: Why are elderly people more sensitive to hydralazine's lupus-like syndrome risk, requiring monitoring of specific laboratory values?
options: Because elderly people are more sensitive to the drug, and red blood cells, lupus erythematosus cell preparation, and antinuclear antibody titer should be determined before starting the drug
Because elderly people are uniformly immune to any lupus-like reaction from hydralazine
Because hydralazine has no known association with lupus-like syndrome in any population
Because laboratory monitoring is unnecessary once therapy has begun regardless of age

stem: The nurse should monitor the elderly client on hydralazine closely for sore throat, fever, and which of the following, notifying the doctor immediately if these occur?
options: Muscle and joint aches and rashes
Improved appetite with no other associated symptom
Enhanced energy level with no other associated symptom
A single episode of mild thirst with no other symptom

stem: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) act to inhibit prostaglandin synthesis, thereby impeding cyclooxygenase, to produce which combined effects?
options: Anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antipyretic effects
Exclusively antipyretic effect with no anti-inflammatory or analgesic action
Exclusively anti-inflammatory effect with no analgesic or antipyretic action
Exclusively analgesic effect with no anti-inflammatory or antipyretic action

stem: Because NSAIDs impair synthesis of renal prostaglandins, they decrease renal blood flow and lead to which outcome, especially in patients with renal or heart failure or liver dysfunction?
options: Reversible renal impairment
A guaranteed improvement in renal blood flow with no risk of impairment
Permanent and irreversible renal failure in every elderly patient regardless of baseline function
An isolated effect limited strictly to hepatic tissue with no renal involvement

stem: Which laboratory values should be monitored in elderly clients on NSAIDs, given the renal and hepatic risks described in the notes?
options: Renal and liver functions and hematocrit
Only serum calcium with no attention to renal or liver function
Only fasting blood glucose with no attention to renal or liver function
Only serum sodium with no attention to renal or liver function

stem: The client must be monitored for symptoms of which type of bleeding while on NSAIDs?
options: Gastro intestinal bleeding
Intracranial hemorrhage exclusively with no mention of GI bleeding
Bleeding limited strictly to surgical wounds with no mention of GI bleeding
Bleeding limited strictly to the urinary tract with no mention of GI bleeding

stem: The drug (NSAID) is absorbed more rapidly when taken with food, milk, or antacids, which increases the tendency for which of the following?
options: Gastro intestinal bleeding
Improved absorption with no increased bleeding risk
A guaranteed decrease in gastric irritation with no bleeding risk
Enhanced renal clearance with no bleeding risk

stem: The client should be taught including blood in vomit, urine, or stool, and coffee ground vomit and black tarry stool, as signs of which complication related to NSAID use?
options: Gastro intestinal bleeding
A normal and expected finding requiring no further action
An isolated dermatologic reaction with no gastrointestinal significance
A sign of improved therapeutic response requiring no further evaluation

stem: Adjustment to the elderly's regular drug regime is frequently made by altering the dose or adding one or more new drugs, which may cause which of the following?
options: Adverse effects that may go unnoticed by the practitioner or unreported especially when cared for at home
A guaranteed absence of any adverse effect regardless of dosage adjustment
An automatic improvement in therapeutic outcome with no risk of adverse reaction
A complete elimination of the need for any further monitoring once a new drug is added

stem: As part of health education of the elderly on drug use, the elderly should be instructed to learn the brand and generic names of all drugs they are taking and which other information?
options: The actions of the drugs they are taking
Only the drug's retail price with no attention to its action
Only the drug's manufacturer with no attention to its action
Only the drug's color with no attention to its action

stem: As part of health education, the elderly should be instructed to report unusual reactions experienced in the past, allergies to foods and other substances, and which of the following?
options: Special medical problems and drugs taken over the last few weeks before being given new drugs
Only their marital status with no attention to allergies or drug history
Only their occupation with no attention to allergies or drug history
Only their preferred hospital with no attention to allergies or drug history

stem: The elderly should be advised to always read the label before taking a drug, to take it exactly as prescribed, and to do which of the following?
options: Never share prescribed drugs with another person
Share prescribed drugs freely with family members who have similar symptoms
Double the prescribed dose whenever symptoms seem to worsen
Discontinue the drug without consulting the doctor whenever symptoms improve

stem: The elderly should be advised not to change brands of a drug without consulting his/her doctor, in order to avoid which of the following?
options: Harmful change in effectiveness, since generic preparations are not equivalent in effect to brand name preparations of some drugs
An automatic improvement in effectiveness regardless of brand switching
A guaranteed absence of any difference between brands of the same drug
A complete elimination of the need for any further monitoring after switching brands

stem: The elderly should be told to check which specific detail on a drug's label before taking it, in addition to storage and labeling precautions?
options: The expiration date
Only the drug's color, with no attention to expiration date
Only the drug's shape, with no attention to expiration date
Only the manufacturer's logo, with no attention to expiration date

stem: The elderly should be advised to safely discard drugs that are outdated or no longer needed, and to keep discarded drugs where?
options: Out of the reach of children
Within easy reach of children for convenience
In an unlocked cabinet accessible to visitors
In a location with no regard for accessibility to children

stem: The elderly should be told to store each drug in its original container, at room temperature, and in places that are NOT accessible to children or exposed to which of the following?
options: Sunlight
Cool, dark storage with no restriction
A refrigerator exclusively regardless of the drug's storage requirement
A locked cabinet exclusively regardless of temperature

stem: The elderly should be advised NOT to mix different drugs in a single container, because relying on memory to identify a drug and specific direction for its use is which of the following?
options: Dangerous
A safe and recommended practice with no risk involved
Required by most pharmacies as standard practice
Beneficial for improving medication adherence with no downside

stem: If the elderly must remove tablets from their original container, the nurse should instruct him/her to use a daily or weekly medication planner as a reminder, including which details on the planner?
options: Drug name, strength, dosage instructions, and physical description
Only the drug's retail price with no other detail
Only the pharmacy's phone number with no other detail
Only the prescribing doctor's signature with no other detail

stem: The elderly should be advised to have a sufficient supply of drugs when traveling, carrying them in which form?
options: In their original containers, and not packed in the luggage
Repackaged into a single unlabeled container for convenience
Packed exclusively in checked luggage with no carry-on copy
Left behind entirely to avoid the inconvenience of travel

stem: Regarding changes in body mass affecting drug therapy in the elderly, total body mass and lean body mass tend to do which of the following with age?
options: Decrease while the proportion of body fat tends to increase
Increase while the proportion of body fat tends to decrease
Remain completely unchanged throughout the aging process
Double in proportion to body fat by age 60

stem: Regarding gastrointestinal function and drug use in the elderly, there is a decrease in gastric acid secretion and gastrointestinal motility in elderly persons, which is known to make it MORE difficult for elderly persons to do which of the following?
options: Absorb drugs than young people
Absorb drugs more rapidly than young people with no difficulty
Eliminate drugs entirely with no absorption occurring at all
Metabolize drugs exclusively through renal pathways with no gastrointestinal involvement

stem: Regarding hepatic function and drug use in the elderly, the liver's ability to metabolize certain drugs decreases with age, due to decreased blood flow to the liver which results from which of the following?
options: An age-related decrease in cardiac output
An age-related increase in cardiac output with no decrease in hepatic blood flow
A complete absence of any change in hepatic blood flow with age
An isolated renal effect with no hepatic involvement

stem: Decreased hepatic function in the elderly may result in more intense drug effects because of which of the following?
options: Higher blood level and a greater risk of drug toxicity caused by prolonged drug effect
A guaranteed decrease in blood level with no risk of toxicity
An automatic improvement in hepatic clearance with age
A complete absence of any change in drug effect duration with age

stem: Regarding renal function and drug use in the elderly, the ability to eliminate some drugs may be reduced by more than what percentage in the elderly, since most drugs used by the elderly are excreted primarily through the kidneys?
If the kidney's ability to excrete a drug is decreased, as found in the elderly, this results in which of the following?
options: High blood levels of the drug and a greater risk of drug toxicity, prolonged blood level, and increased risk of drug toxicity
A guaranteed decrease in blood level with no risk of toxicity
An automatic improvement in renal clearance with age
A complete absence of any change in excretion with age

stem: Regarding disease condition and drug use in the elderly, the physiologic decline or organ function in the elderly is usually worsened by disease conditions, which leads to which of the following?
options: Adverse drug reactions as well as noncompliance
A guaranteed improvement in drug tolerance regardless of disease state
A complete absence of any relationship between disease state and adverse drug reactions
An automatic increase in medication adherence regardless of disease burden

stem: Drug dosage is modified to compensate for age-related decrease in renal function, and which two laboratory values serve as a guide for adjusting drug dosage so that patients receive therapeutic dose without the risk of toxicity?
options: BUN and creatinine level
Only serum sodium and potassium with no mention of BUN or creatinine
Only hemoglobin and hematocrit with no mention of BUN or creatinine
Only fasting blood glucose and HbA1c with no mention of BUN or creatinine

stem: Compared with young people, elderly patients experience adverse drug reactions at approximately which relative frequency, according to the notes?
options: Twice as many adverse drug reactions
Exactly half as many adverse drug reactions
An identical rate of adverse drug reactions with no difference by age
Three times fewer adverse drug reactions than young people

stem: Adverse drug reactions in the elderly are mostly due to greater drug use, poor compliance, and which other factor named in the notes?
options: Physiologic changes
An unrelated increase in physical activity with no bearing on drug reactions
A decrease in the number of prescribed medications with age
An unrelated improvement in dietary habits with no bearing on drug reactions

stem: Because total body water content decreases with age, a normal dosage of which class of drug may result in severe dehydration in an elderly patient?
options: Diuretics
Antacids with no diuretic mechanism
Topical corticosteroids with no systemic fluid effect
Oral rehydration solutions with no diuretic mechanism

stem: A normal dosage of diuretics in the elderly may also lead to raised blood uric acid and glucose level, thereby causing which of the following conflicting conditions?
options: Gout and diabetes mellitus
Hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism exclusively with no mention of gout or diabetes
Osteoporosis and osteoarthritis exclusively with no mention of gout or diabetes
Presbyopia and presbycusis exclusively with no mention of gout or diabetes

stem: When an elderly client is on a diuretic, he/she must be closely monitored for which conflicting metabolic conditions, according to the notes?
options: Gout and diabetes mellitus
Anemia and polycythemia exclusively with no mention of gout or diabetes
Hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism exclusively with no mention of gout or diabetes
Osteoporosis and rickets exclusively with no mention of gout or diabetes

stem: Many elderly people experience light-headedness when taking antihypertensive drugs, which partly decrease elasticity of the blood vessels, because this can lead to which of the following?
options: Lower blood pressure rapidly and insufficient blood flow to the brain which causes dizziness and fainting
A guaranteed increase in blood pressure with no risk of dizziness
An automatic improvement in vascular elasticity regardless of drug therapy
A complete absence of any cerebrovascular effect from antihypertensive therapy

stem: In the elderly, aggressive treatment of high blood pressure may be harmful, and reducing blood pressure to 130/90 mmHg is the target but needs to be done how, compared with younger adults?
options: More slowly in the elderly than young adults
More rapidly in the elderly than young adults
At an identical pace in the elderly and young adults with no difference
Only through surgical intervention in the elderly with no pharmacologic approach

stem: Among the factors linked to noncompliance with drug regimen in elderly patients, which sensory factor is specifically named in the notes?
options: Diminished visual acuity
Enhanced visual acuity with no sensory decline
Improved hearing with age with no sensory decline
An unrelated increase in tactile sensitivity with age

stem: Among the factors linked to noncompliance with drug regimen in elderly patients, which factor relates to the number of medications and route of administration?
options: The need for multiple drugs use in the elderly
A decrease in the total number of prescribed drugs with age
An unrelated improvement in swallowing ability with age
A complete absence of any drug regimen complexity in elderly patients

stem: Among the factors linked to noncompliance, socio-cultural factors may cause elderly patients to do which of the following?
options: Fail to take prescribed doses or to follow the correct schedule
Always follow the prescribed schedule perfectly regardless of cultural background
Experience no influence whatsoever from cultural beliefs about medication
Increase medication adherence uniformly regardless of belief system

stem: To address noncompliance, the nurse should review the elderly person's drug regime with him/her and make sure the elderly understands which specific details about the medication?
options: The dose, the time, and frequency of doses and why the drugs are prescribed
Only the drug's retail price with no attention to dose or frequency
Only the drug's manufacturer with no attention to dose or frequency
Only the drug's color with no attention to dose or frequency

stem: Health education of the elderly on drug use emphasizes that the health care giver caring for the elderly both at home and in institutions must carefully do which of the following?
options: Review the elderly's drugs upon discharge, inform him/her of any potential adverse drug effects to be aware of, and tell him/her to call the nurse/doctor if the effect becomes bothersome
Avoid any discussion of potential adverse drug effects to prevent unnecessary worry
Assume the elderly already understands all potential adverse effects with no further review needed
Delegate all drug education exclusively to family members with no nurse involvement

stem: According to WHO, drugs are defined as which of the following?
options: Any substance or product that is used or intended to be used to modify or explore physiological systems or pathological states for the benefit of the recipient
A substance used exclusively for recreational purposes with no medical benefit
A substance that has no effect whatsoever on biological functions of the body
A substance used exclusively in veterinary medicine with no human application

stem: CASE SCENARIO: An 80-year-old client with severe obstructive coronary artery disease is started on amlodipine besylate. Two days later, she reports worsening chest pain and swelling of her fingers and feet. Which nursing action is MOST appropriate?
options: Notify the doctor immediately, since these are signs of increased anginal frequency and possible heart failure described as risks of this drug
Reassure the client that these symptoms are expected and require no action
Double the amlodipine dose to relieve the chest pain
Withhold all further assessment since the symptoms are unrelated to the new drug

stem: CASE SCENARIO: An elderly client taking atenolol is noted by the nurse to have an apical pulse of 52 beats per minute before the scheduled dose. The client has a history of suspected hyperthyroidism. Which action should the nurse take?
options: Withhold the dose, notify the doctor, and recall that abrupt withdrawal of beta blockers in this client could precipitate thyroid storm, so any change must be gradual
Administer the dose as scheduled regardless of the pulse rate
Double the dose to compensate for the slow pulse
Discontinue the drug abruptly without consulting the doctor

These findings are unrelated to captopril and require no nursing action
The client should double the captopril dose to compensate for fluid loss
The client should be told that fainting is a normal and expected daily occurrence with captopril

options: This is a known first-dose effect of alpha blockers; the client should be placed in a recumbent position, treated supportively, and warned to avoid driving until the drug's CNS effects are known
This reaction means doxazosin must be permanently discontinued after a single dose with no further evaluation
This reaction is unrelated to doxazosin and warrants no special precaution
This reaction indicates the dose should be doubled immediately

stem: CASE SCENARIO: An elderly client on a diuretic for hypertension also has a history of gout, and recent labs show an elevated blood glucose and uric acid level. Which statement BEST reflects the appropriate nursing concern?
options: Diuretics can raise blood uric acid and glucose levels, so the client must be closely monitored for both gout flares and diabetes mellitus
Diuretics have no effect on uric acid or glucose and the findings are unrelated
The elevated glucose and uric acid levels confirm the diuretic should be doubled
Gout and diabetes mellitus cannot coexist as risks from the same medication
